_doc: TOY cross-encoder scoring. A joint [CLS] vector → linear head w·cls+b → sigmoid relevance score. Relevant logit 2.4 → σ≈0.9168; the negation doc logit −1.1 → σ≈0.2497 (the Judge reads the 'not' the Scout missed). Plus a 3×3 query×doc attention matrix (rows sum to 1). REAL ms-marco cross-encoder scores (the 'real'/'contrast' blocks) come from gen_l7_real.py.

real.query: what is the capital of australia

pairRel.doc: Canberra is the capital of Australia

pairBad.doc: Australia is a large country with many cities

real.note: sigmoid of the single relevance logit; eval()+no_grad()+manual_seed(0); committed frozen. The toy block teaches the head arithmetic with a constructed negation; this REAL pair shows the cross-encoder's actual edge — rejecting a keyword-sharing distractor that does not answer.

contrast.query: what is the capital of australia
contrast.docRel: Canberra is the capital of Australia
contrast.docBad: Australia is a large country with many cities
contrast.note: the distractor shares the keyword 'Australia' but does not answer. The bi-encoder (Scout) rates it close to the true answer (narrow gap); the cross-encoder (Judge), reading query+doc together, rejects it (huge gap). biCosBad > crossScoreBad, and the Judge's gap >> the Scout's gap: joint reading discriminates where separate encoding blurs.
